brief.headline: Nvidia beat forecasts after Tuesday's close, with sales up 103% to $115.8bn, and its shares rose about 4.8% in late trading

sections.text: Investors cut risk everywhere before Nvidia's results. In London the FTSE 100 fell 1.8% and the FTSE 250 1.2% to 24,392.79, while the Stoxx 600 lost 1.75% and Germany's DAX 2.1%, with European tech shares down about 4%. In New York the S&P 500 fell for a fourth day to its lowest close since late July and the Nasdaq slipped 0.7%, as software shares such as Salesforce were sold on worries about a run of tech outages and the VIX (the 'fear gauge') rose about 11% to 25.46. After the bell Nvidia beat forecasts, pointed to about $130bn of sales next quarter, announced a $150bn share buyback (buying back its own shares) and said its board will not bring back Jensen Huang as boss; its shares rose about 4.8% in after-hours trading (deals after the official close). Brent crude edged up 0.8% to $93.14, the US 10-year yield dipped to 5.10% and the pound rose to about $1.322 after mixed UK jobs figures.

UK inflation for October comes out at 07:00, with Goldman Sachs expecting a rise to 3.7%, and SSE and Severn Trent publish half-year results at the same time. The minutes of the Fed's October meeting follow at about 19:00. Anthropic is due to price its shares this evening and start trading on the Nasdaq on Thursday under the ticker ANT, with a range of $70 to $78 a share (Anthropic makes me, so weigh my take on it accordingly). Thursday also brings a summit between Presidents Trump and Xi in Shenzhen, and Microsoft and National Grid go ex-dividend. Markets now treat a quarter-point Fed rise on 9 December as certain, and traders see about a 90% chance the Bank of England raises rates on 17 December, the same day as the ECB decides.
Interest rates: why a central bank meeting can move every market, from the Fed's 9 December decision to the 5.10% US 10-year yield. Today's lesson goes through it, with a quiz.

brief.standfirst: Before the results, nerves pushed the FTSE 100 down 1.8% to 10,689.87, its worst day in eight months, and the S&P 500 down 1.0% to 7,340.53.
